LESSON: PROPHETS MENTIONED IN THE QUR’AN VIRTUES OF THE PROPHETS (PATIENCE, HONESTY, TRUTHFULNESS, GENEROSITY AND OBEDIENCE)

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.3: Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience), part of Pillars of Iman in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: how they can apply the virtues of the prophets in their daily life, What virtues do we learn from these prophets?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. mention the twenty-five prophets of Allah (S.W.T.) in the Qur’an,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the virtues of the prophets of Allah for character formation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply the virtues of the prophets of Allah in their daily life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the belief in the prophets of Allah as a Pillar of Iman.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify fellow learners named after prophets,
2. name the prophets of Allah in the Qur’an (Q.4:163-165, 6:84-86, 21: 85-88) and write in their notebook,
3. describe the virtues (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) of the prophets in pairs or small groups, and write the points in their notebook,
4. dramatise/role-play

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Prophets mentioned in the Qur’an Virtues of the Prophets (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity and obedience) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skills of speaking and writing are enhanced as learners name the prophets of Allah

and write them in their notebook.

• Creativity and imagination: the skill is enhanced as learners dramatise/role-play how they can apply the virtues of the

prophets of Allah in their daily life.

• Citizenship: social and civic skills are enhanced as learners discuss the virtues (patience, honesty, truthfulness, generosity

and obedience) of the prophets, in pairs or small groups.

Values:
Social justice equity enhanced as learners dramatise/role-play how they can apply the virtues of the prophets in their daily life.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem as learners name prophets mentioned in the Qur’an.

Link to other learning areas:

Social Studies: as learners discuss the virtues exhibited by the prophets of Allah S.W.T., which is related to good governance.

Main points to remember:

1. mention the twenty-five prophets of Allah (S.W.T.) in the Qur’an,
2. analyse the virtues of the prophets of Allah for character formation,
3. apply the virtues of the prophets of Allah in their daily life,
4. acknowledge the belief in the prophets of Allah as a Pillar of Iman.

Remember the key question: how they can apply the virtues of the prophets in their daily life, What virtues do we learn from these prophets?
